about:
P4 calibration set (docs/p4-spec.md section 6): reactions whose reactive
site is known from the literature, with what ALIE is expected to show,
committed BEFORE ALIE is implemented. Run from the repository root:

cases.name: enolate
cases.reaction: SN2 alkylation with alkyl halides goes to C; hard electrophiles (silyl, acyl) to O

sources.ref: Mayr, Breugst & Ofial (2011) Farewell to the HSAB Treatment of Ambident Reactivity. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 50, 6470-6505

cases.why: ESP points to O; the pilot found ALIE min on the CH2 carbon (5.71 vs 7.47 eV)

cases.name: thiocyanate
cases.reaction: SN2 alkylation gives R-SCN (S); N attack only for highly stabilised carbocations

sources.ref: Loos, Kobayashi & Mayr (2003) Ambident Reactivity of the Thiocyanate Anion Revisited. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 125, 14126-14132
Mayr, Breugst & Ofial (2011) Farewell to the HSAB Treatment of Ambident Reactivity. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 50, 6470-6505

cases.why: ESP points to N; the pilot found ALIE min on S (7.10 vs 8.99 eV)

cases.name: nitrite
cases.reaction: SN2 alkylation gives mainly nitroalkane (N); SN1/Ag+ conditions give alkyl nitrite (O)

sources.ref: Kornblum, Smiley, Blackwood & Iffland (1955) The Mechanism of the Reaction of Silver Nitrite with Alkyl Halides. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 77, 6269
Tishkov, Schmidhammer, Roth, Riedle & Mayr (2005) Ambident Reactivity of the Nitrite Ion Revisited. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 44, 4623-4626
Mayr, Breugst & Ofial (2011) Farewell to the HSAB Treatment of Ambident Reactivity. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 50, 6470-6505

cases.why: the pilot found O 7.86 vs N 7.89 eV: a tie. ALIE must not be claimed to pick N

cases.name: anisole
cases.reaction: EAS on anisole: ortho/para directing, activated

sources.ref: Stock & Brown (1963) A Quantitative Treatment of Directive Effects in Aromatic Substitution. Adv. Phys. Org. Chem. 1, 35-154
Sjoberg, Murray, Brinck & Politzer (1990) Average local ionization energies on the molecular surfaces of aromatic systems as guides to chemical reactivity. Can. J. Chem. 68, 1440-1443

cases.why: ortho/para partial rate factors far exceed meta

cases.name: chlorobenzene
cases.reaction: EAS on chlorobenzene: ortho/para directing, deactivated

sources.ref: Stock & Brown (1963) A Quantitative Treatment of Directive Effects in Aromatic Substitution. Adv. Phys. Org. Chem. 1, 35-154
Sjoberg, Murray, Brinck & Politzer (1990) Average local ionization energies on the molecular surfaces of aromatic systems as guides to chemical reactivity. Can. J. Chem. 68, 1440-1443

cases.why: a halogen deactivates but still directs ortho/para

cases.name: nitrobenzene
cases.reaction: EAS on nitrobenzene: meta directing, strongly deactivated

sources.ref: Stock & Brown (1963) A Quantitative Treatment of Directive Effects in Aromatic Substitution. Adv. Phys. Org. Chem. 1, 35-154
Sjoberg, Murray, Brinck & Politzer (1990) Average local ionization energies on the molecular surfaces of aromatic systems as guides to chemical reactivity. Can. J. Chem. 68, 1440-1443
Murray, Brinck & Politzer (1992) Applications of calculated local surface ionization energies to chemical reactivity. J. Mol. Struct. THEOCHEM 255, 271-281

cases.why: meta is the least deactivated position; a hard case for any one-number descriptor

cases.name: phenoxide
cases.geometry_source: RDKit ETKDG + MMFF94s, seed 0xC0FFEE (an anion: MMFF is a known weak point, see CLAUDE.md)
cases.reaction: phenoxide alkylation: O in aprotic solvents, C(ortho/para) in protic ones

sources.ref: Kornblum, Berrigan & le Noble (1963) Solvation as a Factor in the Alkylation of Ambident Anions. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 85, 1141-1147

cases.why: the solvent decides, so no single ground-state number should be read as the answer
